articles.headline: Red Safe Code in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Following Orders
keyFacts: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 features a locked red safe in the cabinet of the third campaign mission, Following Orders.
Players can unlock the red safe by entering the code 214 or by shooting at it directly.
Opening the safe yields a collectible note for achievement progress and an illegal contraband item.
body: Following Orders is the third mission of the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 ‘s campaign, and you can find a red safe. Once you find the safe, you can open it with the correct code, but the game doesn’t necessarily tell you where to find it or what the code is.
In this guide, I will help you figure out where the red safe is located and how to crack it open.
Table of contents
How to find the Red Safe in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Following Orders
Red Safe Code in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4
How to find the Red Safe in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Following Orders

When the mission begins, you’ll find yourself interrogating a couple to find where the defector is. Instead of interrogating them, head to the room on the right. It’s the first room on the right when you enter the house.

Screenshot by Destructoid Head inside, open the cabinet, and you’ll find the Red Safe over there. When you find it for the first time, it remains locked. You can simply shoot at it, but using a code is the easier way to get it done.
Red Safe Code in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4
The correct code is “214”. This code is the same for all scenarios, and it will open the safe. You have to use your arrow keys (assuming you’re on PC like me) to scroll and input the code.
Screenshot by Destructoid Inside, you’ll find two items.
A note. There are four notes you can find in this mission, and it’s one of them. Finding and reading 50 notes allows you to make progress towards one of the in-game achievements.
A contraband. These are illegal items that you can find in the campaign, and they’re also part of the in-game campaign.
Once again, you can complete the mission without opening the safe, but I liked how it fits in the lore.

articles.headline: Bucs offensive tackle reaches 709 snaps without surrendering a sack
keyFacts: Buccaneers offensive tackle Luke Goedeke has reached 709 consecutive snaps without surrendering a sack, the second-longest active NFL streak.
Goedeke moved to right tackle after struggling during his rookie season at left guard following the 2022 draft.
His pass blocking allows the offense to send more receivers into routes instead of using extra blockers to protect Jalon Daniels.
body: Offensive tackles are often judged by their worst plays. One missed assignment, one lost rep, or one breakdown in protection can completely change a game. For Luke Goedeke, those costly moments have become increasingly rare, and his latest accomplishment puts him in impressive company across the NFL. Goedeke currently holds the second-longest active streak among offensive tackles without allowing a sack, having gone 709 consecutive snaps without surrendering a sack. Only Denver Broncos left tackle Garett Bolles sits ahead of him with 1,077 snaps. Goedeke's streak also places him comfortably ahead of Anthony Belton (473), Roger Rosengarten (404), Lane Johnson (374) and Tyler Guyton (324).

The accomplishment is particularly impressive, given that Goedeke's career began in Tampa Bay. Originally drafted in the second round of the 2022 NFL Draft, Goedeke struggled during his rookie season at left guard before finding his footing after moving back to his natural position at right tackle. What initially looked like a questionable investment has developed into one of Jason Licht's more successful offensive line decisions. His development has become especially important given Tampa Bay's reliance on its offensive tackles to hold up in pass protection. With Tristan Wirfs protecting the left side, Goedeke gives the Buccaneers a pair of tackles capable of handling difficult assignments without consistently requiring additional help from tight ends or running backs.

That flexibility matters for offensive coordinator Zac Robinson, particularly with rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels operating the offense. When tackles can survive isolated matchups against opposing edge rushers, the offense has more freedom to release additional receivers into routes rather than keeping extra blockers near the formation. However, the streak shouldn't be confused with Goedeke never losing a pass-blocking rep. Pressures and quarterback hits can still occur without resulting in sacks, and sacks themselves are influenced by quarterback movement, time to throw, and protection responsibilities. What makes 709 consecutive snaps significant is the consistency required to avoid allowing the most damaging outcome over such an extended stretch. Goedeke's emergence also speaks to the importance of patience in player development. The same offensive lineman who struggled to establish himself at guard has become one of Tampa Bay's most dependable players at tackle.

articles.headline: 'Remarkably close to the minimum permitted by physics': this superconducting memory bit runs at an estimated 5x the limit, but at -269°C the fridge shrinks its claimed million-fold edge over today’s chips considerably
keyFacts: Hebrew University physicists led by Yonathan Anahory estimated that a superconducting vortex bit operates at five times Landauer's limit.
The university claimed a million-fold efficiency edge over conventional computers, though this figure disregards cooling costs at 4.2 kelvin.
A peer reviewer opposed publication, arguing the researchers inferred work using simulations rather than directly measuring bit erasure.
body: - Hebrew University physicists estimate a single superconducting vortex can act as a memory bit at about five times Landauer's limit, at 4.2 kelvin
- The fivefold figure is a simulation-based estimate anchored to continuous-drive measurements, not a measured erasure, however
- The release's million-fold edge over conventional computers disregards refrigeration costs

Every time a computer erases a bit, it pays an energy toll that physics will not waive; IBM physicist Rolf Landauer pinned down the minimum in 1961: kT ln 2, a figure that scales with temperature and works out to about 2.9 zeptojoules at room temperature.
No real chip comes close, making that gap a favorite target as computing's electricity bill keeps climbing.
Physicists at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem now say they have come within about five times of that floor using a single superconducting vortex, a nanoscale whirlpool of electrical current.
Storing a bit in a whirlpool might be a slightly controversial play

The work, published in Nature Communications on September 24 and publicized in a university release on October 11, is a clever measurement, but it has limitations: the device works only at liquid-helium temperatures, and one of the paper's three peer reviewers has opposed the final version.
In a thin superconducting film, a magnetic field can punch through in tiny tubes, each ringed by circulating current and carrying one quantum of flux, and these vortices snag on defects.

The team, led by Yonathan Anahory, used a 55-nanometer niobium film patterned into a strip 10 micrometers wide and cooled to 4.2 kelvin. Sweeping a steady current through the strip nudged individual vortices into spots where the film's natural disorder offers two neighboring resting places only a few nanometers apart. The positioning matters here, acting effectively as a store of value: left or right becomes zero or one.

They then rocked each vortex with an alternating current and tracked it with a SQUID-on-tip microscope, a magnetic sensor built onto a tapered glass probe. The part of the motion that lags behind the push reveals how much energy is lost each cycle.

Anahory said the result puts the bit at roughly five times Landauer's limit, “bringing it remarkably close to the minimum permitted by physics.” The release covers the energy as measured for the actual test, not the cooling aspect, which could significantly reduce the efficiency story here.

The paper adds another caveat here: Its abstract concedes that “our experimental method requires a steady sinusoidal drive incompatible with Landauer’s erasure protocol” and attributes the near-limit figure to numerical analysis.

The lab measured dissipation while vortices were wiggled back and forth continuously; the cost of a true erasure, forcing a bit of unknown value into a known state, was estimated with simulations anchored to that data. The fivefold number is the authors' estimate for a working bit driven at 150 kHz, spelled out in their replies to reviewers.
This has, however, spurred a peer review fight, also published by Nature Communications, which lists the unusually blunt referee reports alongside the paper.

Reviewer #2 rejected the first draft, said the second could run only with extra experiments, and recommended against the final version, opening with “Authors write that they measure work. It is not true.” The reviewer argued that force, displacement, and work were estimated or inferred rather than observed, and asked for two sanity checks: show the vortex being pushed into one well and staying there, and show its spontaneous hopping changing with temperature, as thermal activation predicts.
The authors declined both, citing scanning drift that limits static imaging to about 20 nanometers and noting that changing temperature also reshapes the pinning landscape.

Reviewer #3 backed publication, calling the work original and sound and warning that the extra experiments could delay it indefinitely. Reviewer #1 judged the technique ill-suited to erasure at useful speeds and encouraged a more modest title.
Speed is the tradeoff

Not only is the cost of cooling unaccounted for, with real-world refrigeration costs not being factored in, but the bigger problem is also speed. Landauer's limit is only reachable if you take your time, and work by Proesmans, Ehrich, and Bechhoefer shows that the extra cost of erasure rises as operations speed up.
The Hebrew University estimate applies at 150 kHz, or essentially one operation every 6.7 microseconds, while superconducting logic chips were clocked at 6 GHz more than a decade ago.
Going slower does not help either. By the authors' own noise data, the two wells central to the near-limit result let the vortex hop on its own roughly 3,000 to 7,000 times a second at 4.2 K.

The authors argue that this is fine as long as operations run much faster than the hopping. But it means the most efficient wells hold information for well under a millisecond, and the paper does not show a single well that is both near the limit and able to keep data for long.

The tradeoff, therefore, is one between speed, cost, and durability, and given that the use case is data storage, it is a tough call to make. Vortex memory is not entirely new; the Hebrew University contribution is energy accounting, and its claim to a first is narrow, though it uses a single vortex.

The Hebrew University team has produced a careful, somewhat contested estimate of how cheaply a single vortex can be shuffled between two spots, and a reminder that sitting close to the physical limit and being efficient at the wall socket are very different things.

articles.headline: How the Packers’ defense is pressuring into interceptions
keyFacts: The Green Bay Packers defense improved its league ranking from 26th to 14th after forcing five turnovers in Week 5.
Packers defensive players Xavier McKinney and Ty'Ron Hopper intercepted three total passes against quarterbacks Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum.
The Packers defense will play against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night in Green Bay.
body: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers defense is climbing out of the bottom of the NFL’s worst defenses after a lopsided Week 3 loss to the Falcons, turning in a five-turnover performance in Week 5. They ranked 26th in EPA per play after Week 3 and now rank 14th after Week 5.

While their run defense EPA per play and run defense success rate allowed remain below league average, the Packers defense is surviving on the strength of their pass defense. In week five, they forced Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum into three interceptions.

The quality of quarterbacks faced might not be anything but below average, but the pass coverage unit shows on tape that they are sound in their assignments regardless, meaning they don’t give up ground or space easily within their play calls.
First interception
The first interception came with 5:39 remaining in the first quarter on a 2nd-and-10. Tyson Bagent was the Bears starter this game until Keenum took over late in the game.
Bagent brought the offense out in an 11 personnel shotgun formation to run a 3×1 dagger concept Ben Johnson has used to carve up opposing teams in the secondary.

The Packers are playing cover-8 “trix” once the formation motions to a 3×1. In cover-8, the coverage plays cover-2 to the trips passing strength while the backside safety keys in on the final #3 receiver or the deepest crossing route.

Luther Burden is the receiver sent in motion running the dig route from behind the bunch receivers who are running deeper crossing routes across the field. Bagent is looking for the dig route and tried to rip the pass over Javon Bullard gaining depth in the vertical hook under the dig.
Bullard tipped the pass up, allowing safety Xavier McKinney to run under the tipped ball from his deep half safety zone.
Second interception
Bagent’s second interception came with 41 seconds left in the third quarter and down 23-7 on a pass intended for Colston Loveland. The pass was intercepted by McKinney again.

The Bears started in an empty 3×2 formation with trips to the right. Bagent is targeting Loveland running the dig route on a two receiver wrap concept with a short curl route under the dig. The intent is to pull up the curl flat player to the curl route and hit the dig in the window between the curl flat and weak hook defender.
The Packers are playing cover-3 strong buzz rotation with the safety buzzing down to the strong hook toward the nickel, what Gannon would “Ralph” rotation (rotation to the right to the nickel).
McKinney, as the strong hook defender, reads Bagent’s eyes the whole way and with no one threatening his zone, McKinney works to the middle of the field to play the pass to Loveland.
Bagent is late on the throw, has to try to fit the pass over the hook defender, and throws it too far in front of Loveland and right into the hands of McKinney, who started from the far hash.
Third interception

The third interception came with 12:58 left in the 4th quarter. Case Keenum was in for Bagent, who drove the offense into the red zone before turning it over on a hurried throw with pressure in his face.

The Bears were in an empty 3×2 formation again here on 4th and goal from the 9-yard line. Keenum tried to hit Rome Odunze on a double move over the middle but Ty’Ron Hopper came racing over from his quarter/flat zone to intercept the pass.

The defense is in red zone quarters where they first show pressure and a cover-0 look. Hopper and Zaire Franklin back out of the blitz but Keenum is already changing the protection to slide right in case he gets a free runner off his right edge.

The result is disastrous, though. The protection slide away from Lukas Van Ness proved to be costly. Van Ness came off the offense’s left edge untouched as the left tackle took his block inside to the inside rusher. Van Ness forced Keenum to drift away from the pocket and throw across his body to Odunze.
Hopper read his eyes the whole way and came over from his zone to make the interception at the goal line where he eventually returned it out to the 20-yard line.

The Packers coverage will be tested on Sunday night as the Cowboys come into Green Bay eager to get back on track after a brutal loss to the Buccaneers in week 5. The Cowboys like to throw deep, and the combination of CeeDee Lamb and Dak Prescott is nothing to scoff at.

articles.headline: Jets need one thing to pull off an unexpected win over Patriots
keyFacts: The 2-3 New York Jets will play a critical Week 6 divisional matchup against the New England Patriots.
ESPN reporter Rich Cimini stated the Jets need takeaways rather than just sacks to pull off an upset.
Cimini said the Jets' goal is to pressure Patriots quarterback Drake Maye into making costly mistakes.
body: The New York Jets are 2-3 so far this season and No. 3 in the AFC East. They obviously have a tough division, with the Buffalo Bills and New England Patriots ahead of them. That's what makes this Week 6 matchup against the Patriots so critical.

The Jets haven't been contenders for a long time. Head coach Aaron Glenn and the team want to get New York back into that winning category. Pulling off a huge upset of the Patriots would be one way to not only do that but also get the attention of the rest of the NFL.
So, the stakes are high. The Jets need to successfully do one thing to pull off an upset, according to an NFL analyst.
The New York Jets need to force Drake Maye into costly mistakes to have a chance against the New England Patriots

ESPN has released its Week 6 preview ahead of the weekend of games, and in it, reporter Rich Cimini says that for the Jets to win, they need "takeaways." Sacks help, too, but he says they'll need to do more than that.

"After sacking the Browns' Deshaun Watson eight times last week, what can the Jets do for an encore?" he asks in the piece, adding that coordinator Brian Duker joked about upping that to nine against the Patriots.

"To pull the upset, the Jets need takeaways, not sacks. The Jets have only one interception," Cimini states in the feature. "Their goal is to pressure QB Drake Maye into bad decisions, getting him to revert to his early-season funk -- when he threw six interceptions in the first three games."
Bad decisions are always a good thing when it's the other team making them. That's what the Jets hope to see against the Patriots in Week 6.

articles.headline: Brazil: Amazon deforestation lowest in nearly 40 years
keyFacts: According to space agency Inpe, Amazon deforestation in Brazil dropped nearly 42 percent to reach its lowest recorded level since 1988.
The Amazon is the world's largest tropical rainforest, where deforestation and illegal exploitation have pushed the ecosystem closer to a climate tipping point.
President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva stated the goal is to achieve zero illegal deforestation by 2030 ahead of the October runoff election.
body: Brazil has recorded the lowest level of deforestation in the Amazon rainforest in nearly 40 years.

According to data released by the Brazilian space research agency Inpe on Friday, between August 2025 and July 2026, 3,335 square kilometers (1,288 square miles) of forest were cleared, the lowest level witnessed since records began in 1988.
The numbers showed a nearly 42% decrease from last year's figure of 5,731 square kilometers.
The Amazon is the world's largest tropical rainforest and one of its most biodiverse ecosystems, most of which lies in Brazil.
It also extends into parts of Peru, Colombia and other South American countries. Deforestation and the illegal exploitation of resources have been pushing it closer to a climate tipping point.
Drop hailed as 'historic achievement'
"It's an absolutely stratospheric drop...it's like a dream," said Environment Minister Joao Paulo Capobianco at a press conference in the capital, Brasilia.
"Our goal is to achieve zero illegal deforestation by 2030," said President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a post on X.
"The figures released today are a historic achievement," said Marcio Astrini, executive secretary at climate advocacy group Observatorio do Clima.

"They put Brazil at the forefront of the forest protection agenda and show the world that, with political will, it is possible to stop the chainsaws and curb greenhouse gas emissions," Astrini said on his organization's website.

Observatorio do Clima said the figures were the result of a "sustained commitment" to protecting the environment by the government, which introduced greater monitoring and stiffer penalties for illegal logging.
The news comes ahead of the October 25 runoff election between Lula and conservative senator Flavio Bolsonaro with the two running neck and neck according to polls.

articles.headline: Who might be the next White House press secretary after Katie Zacharia’s exit
keyFacts: The White House announced Katie Zacharia will transition out of her press secretary role less than a week after taking the job.
Potential successors being discussed include Scott Jennings, Anna Kelly, Elizabeth Pipko, Stephen Miller, Katie Miller, and Steven Cheung.
President Donald Trump told Fox News that he has no short list and is in no hurry to choose Zacharia's replacement.
body: A pile of candidates is already being tossed around as possible replacements for Katie Zacharia , hours after she was ousted as White House press secretary .

The White House announced Zacharia would “transition” out of the job on Friday, less than one week after she stepped into the role as Karoline Leavitt’s replacement. Zacharia’s departure from Washington comes after she faced intense scrutiny during her short tenure as press secretary for President Donald Trump. Critics mocked Zacharia’s performance during her first and last press conference on Tuesday, and ripped her for describing herself as an attorney, despite having never passed the bar exam.
Trump appears to be in little hurry to pick a replacement, telling Fox News Friday he believes the White House has been operating fine since Leavitt left, and that he has no short list.
Here’s who the president might be interviewing next to fill the open press secretary role.
Top contenders on betting markets
Three possible contenders are leading the pack on Kalshi.

As of Friday afternoon, CNN political commentator Scott Jennings is first at 19%, followed by principal deputy White House press secretary Anna Kelly at 18% and former Republican National Committee national spokeswoman Elizabeth Pipko at 11%.
Jennings is known as a conservative commentator on CNN who has been praised by Trump.
Kelly served as a spokeswoman for Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign before joining the White House. She previously worked for the RNC and Rep. Derrick Van Orden (R-WI).
Pipko, the author of Finding My Place , was spokeswoman for the RNC in 2024, after working on Trump’s presidential campaign.
Internal White House picks
Aside from Kelly, there are several other names rumored as possible options for press secretary who are already working on the president’s team.
Both White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller and his wife, Katie, have been speculated as possible successors to Zacharia.
Stephen Miller has been senior adviser to Trump for years, and is particularly known for pushing strong views on immigration policy.

Katie Miller once served as former Vice President Mike Pence’s communications director and has held several other government roles, including one of the first advisers named to Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency. She now runs a podcast geared toward conservatives, where she routinely interviews major figures in Washington, such as Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio .

White House communications director Steven Cheung has a long and close history with Trump, having held senior roles on all three of his presidential campaigns. Cheung’s political career goes back decades, when he once held an intern position in former California Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger’s office.
From the Cabinet agencies

Tricia McLaughlin was the Department of Homeland Security’s senior spokeswoman under the Trump administration until February. Prior to that, she served in various senior communications advisory roles in Ohio politics, including for now-gubernatorial nominee Vivek Ramaswamy and Gov. Mike DeWine (R-OH).

Kingsley Wilson has been the Department of War‘s press secretary since May 2025. She previously had stints at the Center for Renewing America and Trump’s 2020 campaign, among other positions. However, she held only one press conference during her tenure at the department, in December 2025. Her father is Steve Cortes, a campaign spokesman during Trump’s 2016 and 2020 bids.
Other names

Alina Habba could be in line to be interviewed. Habba was once Trump’s personal attorney as he navigated complex legal battles. The president later picked her to become acting U.S. attorney for the District of New Jersey. Habba resigned from that position last December.
TRUMP TRANSITIONING KATIE ZACHARIA OUT OF PRESS SECRETARY ROLE — BUT WILL KEEP SUSIE WILES

Although likely an unserious candidate, Laura Loomer has floated herself as a successor to Zacharia. The media personality is known for stirring interparty squabbles in Washington circles and holds a strong following on social media.
“I would be an amazing Press Secretary. I’d show President Trump all the receipts. I would bring my binder full of receipts to every briefing,” Loomer said .

articles.headline: Katie Zacharia’s five days as press secretary expose flaws in Trump’s TV-driven hiring
keyFacts: The White House confirmed Katie Zacharia is leaving her role as press secretary after five days following criticism of her briefings and credentials.
Commentators stated that Zacharia's quick exit illustrates flaws in President Donald Trump's practice of hiring officials based on television appearances.
The report noted a search is presumed to be underway for Zacharia's successor as White House press secretary.
body: And so Katie Zacharia joins the mayfly ranks of Liz Truss, Anthony Scaramucci, New Coke, CNN+ and Quibi. To say she burned twice as bright and half as long would be too kind. She went out like a firework on a soggy night.

The White House confirmed on Friday that Zacharia is leaving her role as press secretary after just five days on the job. No one was surprised after a lacklustre press briefing debut and scrutiny over her legal credentials.
But even more importantly, Zacharia lived by the sword and died in the one arena that Donald Trump truly cares about: television.

She reportedly got the job by closely monitoring the US president’s public schedule and tracked his active hours on Truth Social to predict exactly when he would be watching TV. She then timed her own appearances on air to make sure she caught his eye. The fact that she fitted the glossy blond aesthetic from what Trump calls “central casting” also helped.

But TV also proved her undoing. On Thursday, Zacharia gave a series of interviews to Trump-friendly outlets in a desperate bid for redemption. Instead, she sealed her own fate with more hapless performances.

She must have expected Fox News host Sean Hannity, who has even spoken at Trump rallies, to give her an easy ride. But even he was sceptical when she admitted she had “stepped up to the plate with very little prep time” for the first briefing. Hannity asked: “Am I hearing that you think the staff should have prepped you better?”

Zacharia rejected the notion that she had only taken questions from conservative outlets, incorrectly asserting that the Daily Mail is “not known to be a conservative outlet”. Hannity also quizzed her about her dubious legal credentials. “Why not just say, ‘I went to Pepperdine law school, and then took a different career path, and I took the bar once and didn’t pass?’”

Zacharia tried again on Fox & Friends but ran into host Lawrence Jones, who said: “You know, Katie, it’s been a tough week for you. It’s not an easy job to be the press secretary and you never want to be the story.”
He also asked: “Do you think you still have the confidence of the president?” Zacharia responded, “I’m standing here,” referring to the fact that she was speaking from the White House north lawn.
Her exit hours later was met with widespread ridicule – and a measure of human compassion for someone whom Trump had subjected to a very public humiliation.
Scaramucci, who lasted only 11 days as White House communications director during Trump’s first term, tweeted: “Records are made to be broken. But I take no pleasure in other people’s pain.”

Joe Lockhart, a former White House press secretary under Bill Clinton, said in a phone interview: “It’s hard to generate sympathy for this woman, but there was no way for her to succeed. It takes years to be ready to do that job. Not days, not hours. I spent 20 years preparing for my first briefing from the very first campaign I did. It was very unfair for her, but very bad judgment on her part to think she could wander out there and smile.”

The fiasco was also a reminder of Trump’s woeful judgment as a manager whose chief criteria are looks and loyalty. During his 2015 presidential campaign, he promised that he would only hire “the best people”, comparing his future administration to corporate boardrooms. His first national security adviser, Michael Flynn, resigned after 23 days.

His second term has featured incompetents such as Kristi Noem, fired as homeland security secretary after multiple controversies, Robert F Kennedy Jr, a health secretary who spent years promoting anti-scientific claims about vaccine safety, and Pete Hegseth, a defence secretary who bungled the Iran war and announced a livestreamed execution only to be overruled by his boss.

Kurt Bardella, a political commentator, said: “It shows the limitations of the president making decisions like this based solely on, ‘oh, I liked watching this clip of her on this segment in the most friendly environment possible.’ We’ve seen this time and again with this president selecting figures for very meaningful, important and substantive positions solely based on cable news, and just look at how the war in Iran is going to know that ain’t working out too good.”

Trump also entrusted tech bro Elon Musk to take a chainsaw to the federal government. His choice of personnel has had damaging consequences for US institutions. The position of White House press secretary is the latest example.

Lockhart added: “It one more time shows how Trump cheapens everything he touches. He wants everything to be in his image. He tears down the East Wing. He puts his name on the Kennedy Center. Now he has tried to put someone in that job who reflects him, not the country and the values and the power of this country.

“He has cheapened another institution. I hold that room somewhat dear, and it’s sad to watch each of these things get remade in his image because he is cheap, tawdry, corrupt, and he has managed to make the United States reflect those values around the world rather than the ones we knew about for 250 years before him.”

Zacharia will survive and maybe thrive as a “former White House press secretary” in rightwing media, just as Scaramucci still makes the most of his “former” title. Meanwhile, the hunt is on, presumably, for a successor who can at least look reporters in the eye and not get into a tangle about their credentials.

But the cold truth is that the job of White House press secretary is superfluous when Trump is a word machine who holds two-hour campaign rallies, turns social media into a stream of consciousness and takes calls from reporters on his mobile phone. Playing the role of Trump’s spokesperson carries the inherent risk of inadvertently factchecking him.

“He’s certainly remade the job because all the press secretary does now is repeat what the president says and tell him how brilliant he was in saying it,” Lockhart concluded. “It used to be that credibility was the currency in the room. It’s impossible to be credible when you’re working for someone who lies almost every time he speaks.”

articles.headline: How to lose a job in five days
keyFacts: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia was fired on Friday after serving only five days in her position.
Her dismissal makes her the shortest-tenured White House press secretary in history.
NBC's Garrett Haake stated that the firing demonstrates a White House struggling with messaging weeks before the midterm elections.
body: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia speaks during a news briefing at the White House on October 13, 2026. | Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images
This story appeared in The Logoff , a daily newsletter that helps you stay informed about the Trump administration without letting political news take over your life. Subscribe here .
Welcome to The Logoff: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia is out of a job after only five days.

What happened? Zacharia was fired on Friday after less than a week in her new role, after a rocky start that included a halting performance in the briefing room, a scandal over her legal credentials, and a round of less-than-successful cleanup interviews .

The firing makes her the shortest-tenured White House press secretary in history, outstripping even first-term Trump communications director Anthony Scaramucci, who made it 10 or 11 days (figures vary) before getting the boot.

“Records are made to be broken,” Scaramucci posted on Friday . “But I take no pleasure in other people’s pain.” (No word yet on whether the “Zacharia” will emerge as a unit of time, as the “Scaramucci” has.)

What’s the context? Zacharia’s remarkably short stint behind the podium unfolded as the White House is engaged in an unprecedented attack on press freedom: The administration is still trying to ban three media outlets — CNN, MS NOW, and Politico — from the White House, though as of earlier this week, a judge is still blocking the ban from taking effect.
The diminished nature of the press secretary job was on full display in Zacharia’s sole briefing on Tuesday , when she took questions from just three outlets: Breitbart, Fox News, and the Daily Mail.

Why does this matter? Zacharia’s no good, very bad week is not likely to leave much of a lasting mark in its own right — other than, perhaps, as pub trivia — but as NBC’s Garrett Haake points out , it’s a very tangible manifestation of a White House that seems to have no idea how to spin itself out of crisis with just weeks until the midterm elections.
Most recently, Trump has landed on flat-out lying about the state of the economy — but like Zacharia’s time as press secretary, it doesn’t seem like it’s going to go all that well .
And with that, it’s time to log off…
The underlying trend — municipal inaction — may be infuriating, but I loved this story about “tactical urbanism” from my colleague Sara Herschander.

As she writes, vigilante activists have taken to painting their own crosswalks, building benches, and even installing makeshift bike lanes in their neighborhoods — and every time they do, “they remind us that it is not actually that hard — or even that expensive — to do many of the simple things that can make our cities safer and more pleasant places to live.”
You can read Sara’s full piece here , no gift link needed. Enjoy, have a great weekend, and we’ll see you on Monday!

articles.headline: Solly March set for surprise EFL transfer two months after Premier League plea
keyFacts: Reports state former Brighton winger Solly March is set to join Championship club Charlton Athletic as a free agent.
March previously stated in August that he believed he was still capable of playing in the Premier League.
Charlton manager Nathan Jones previously worked with March as an assistant and caretaker manager at Brighton.
body: Solly March is reportedly set to sign for Charlton Athletic following his summer exit from Brighton.
The winger made 300 appearances and scored 26 goals across a 13-year spell at the Seagulls.
March is heading back to the Championship with Charlton months after ending his 13-year stint with Brighton Getty
March was part of the side that finished as runners-up in the 2016/17 Championship to earn promotion to the Premier League .
Knee injuries blighted the latter years of his time on the south coast, and he has remained a free agent since the window shut.
However, as per various reports, the 32-year-old is heading back to the Championship by signing for Charlton .
The Addicks are 13th in the standings and managed by the animated Nathan Jones , who worked with the player at Brighton.
Jones was assistant to Oscar Garcia and oversaw March’s senior debut for the club.
When Sami Hyypia resigned as manager in December 2014, the now-Charlton boss played March on two occasions as Brighton caretaker.
What did March say on his future after Brighton exit?
Throughout his spell at Brighton, March played on both wings and in midfield, and even had a brief spell at left-back.
His versatility played a key role in the club becoming an established Premier League side that now competes in Europe.
However, whilst he has plenty of Championship experience thanks to his 75 appearances in the division, he was keen to stay at the top.
March told talkSPORT towards the end of the summer window that he is still capable of playing in the Premier League Getty
“For me personally, I still want to play in the Premier League,” he told talkSPORT in August, whilst also dismissing a move abroad.
“I definitely think I can do that. Maybe I’ve got to be patient, I don’t know. But it’s difficult, you get itchy feet, you’re at home alone and training alone.”
March added: “I can play many positions.
“I think I’ve got quality that maybe a lot of Premier League teams don’t have, and I think the experience helps.
“When you’ve played 300 games, you know what it’s like, and you can help the younger players and advise them.
“I still think I’ve got the quality… I’m feeling good, the best I have in two years. Just waiting for the right chance, and I think patience is the key.”

articles.headline: The Cyberpunk 2077 movie won't be 'a film adaptation of the game,' CD Projekt chief says
keyFacts: CD Projekt co-CEO Michał Nowakowski stated that the company is partnering with Paramount Pictures on a live-action Cyberpunk film project.
Nowakowski said the movie will tell a story in the Cyberpunk world rather than a direct adaptation of the game.
Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 is scheduled to debut on Netflix on October 20.
body: We learned last week that a Cyberpunk 2077 movie is in the works, an announcement I used mainly to talk about a completely different cyberpunk movie starring Keanu Reeves as a guy named Johnny who's having a bad week. Now we've got a bit more insight into what CD Projekt Red has in mind for the film, and it's possible that a guy named Johnny may not be involved at all.

"Our contract with Anonymous Content expired, and in the meantime, an opportunity arose to establish cooperation with Paramount Pictures," co-CEO Michał Nowakowski told Polish PAP Biznes (Google translated), referring to the Cyberpunk 2077 "live action project" that was announced in 2023 and ultimately went nowhere. "We decided that we would conduct a live-action Cyberpunk project in a new formula.

"At this point, we can only say that we definitely don't want to make a film adaptation of the game. We want to tell a story in the world of Cyberpunk, but it won't be a one-to-one translation of the game's story."

I loved Cyberpunk 2077, and the fact that it featured two Hollywood stars in central roles might make it seem like a natural fit for a direct translation. But I think avoiding that approach is the wiser move: V's story has been told, and trying to replicate it on film only invites unflattering comparisons and criticism. And it's not as though the world of Night City is short of other stories to tell, after all, nor would it be difficult to indirectly tie it to the game through references or cameos, if the urge to do so is really that strong.

Remember as well that two of the most successful game-to-screen adaptations, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners and Resident Evil, took their respective underlying settings and made them their own. That's basically what Cyberpunk 2077 is, as far as that goes: A vision of Mike Pondsmith's Cyberpunk tabletop setting, interpreted through the lens of a new timeline. They're all stronger for it, because they allow creators to work within a particular framework without tying them to specifics.
It's way too early in the process to say when all of this big-screen fun will actually happen, but Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 is set to debut on Netflix on October 20.

articles.headline: 8 Call of Duty Games Still Missing from Game Pass
keyFacts: Polygon reported that eight classic Call of Duty games are still missing from the Xbox Game Pass subscription service.
The missing titles include several popular franchise entries such as Call of Duty: Black Ops, World at War, and Modern Warfare Remastered.
The article does not state when or if Microsoft plans to add these remaining classic Call of Duty games to Game Pass.
body: The franchise has slipped from its lofty perch in recent years, but there was a time when the launch of a new Call of Duty game was a huge event. The anticipation was never quite on the level of Grand Theft Auto 6, but the series reliably mattered in a way that many other games did not.

When Microsoft purchased Activision, some of us assumed we wouldn’t have to wait long before being able to play all of those classic games on Xbox Game Pass. Why else would Microsoft drop that kind of money on the company, if not to leverage its library of classics? But Call of Duty has made only a weak showing on the subscription service since then, with many of its most iconic games still available only for purchase. With Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launching Oct. 23, here are eight Call of Duty games somehow still missing from Game Pass. We’d love to see them get added soon.
8 Call of Duty: Black Ops
Released: Nov. 9, 2010

After Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, it was unclear how the franchise might top itself. Then came Call of Duty: Black Ops, with an energetic campaign that included outrageous moments such as an attempted assassination of Fidel Castro. Some of the most memorable characters in the franchise experienced a thrilling campaign, and that was just for starters. Without Black Ops, we never would have been introduced to the Nuketown map so many of us know and love from multiplayer deathmatch. The game’s absence from Game Pass is an injustice.
7 Call of Duty: World at War
Released: Nov. 10, 2008

World at War once again told a compelling story set in World War 2, like most of the franchise entries up to that point, but that’s not why most players remember it fondly. Rather, they recall the zombies mode, which developer Treyarch introduced to the overall franchise with sufficient success that it quickly became a standard component in future titles. Players worked to cooperate against increasingly powerful waves of invading zombies, rushing from one site to another and struggling to survive against the endless horde. If you love fighting zombies in Call of Duty, you owe that mode to this one great game, which is sadly missing from Game Pass. And if you want more World War 2 action of a more recent vintage, there’s always 2017’s Call of Duty: WW2.
6 Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare
Released: Nov. 4, 2014

There’s a popular meme you might have seen: “Press F to pay respects.” The familiar line comes from Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare. Early in the campaign, wounded during a recent military operation and now missing one arm, you attend the funeral of a fallen comrade. As you look over the coffin, text prompts you to press a button to grieve. Also present at that funeral: Jonathan Irons, the father of the slain soldier. Voiced by Kevin Spacey, Irons plays a pivotal role in a story that explores the contentious relationship between private enterprise and the United States government. It’s an intriguing tale, over-the-top in the way some of the best Call of Duty campaigns so often were, even if it occasionally feels contrived. Modern players are missing out on an experience that’s still worth having.
5 Call of Duty: Ghosts
Released: Nov. 4, 2013

Many players associated Infinity Ward with the best Call of Duty had to offer, even though there were three studios working on the series. Following the very noisy exit of Vince Zampella and Jason West in 2010, the remaining team had to work hard to prove they still had the creative juice necessary to build something special. Call of Duty: Ghosts was the result of their effort. Co-developed with Neversoft (Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater) and Raven Software, the game suffered from slower pacing and less interesting maps, but still managed to pack in some of the high-octane sequences for which the franchise is known. Although it’s not remembered as a high point for the series, it provided a solid experience that today’s players can still enjoy a great deal, provided they keep their expectations in check.
4 Call of Duty: Black Ops 2
Released: Nov. 13, 2012

Call of Duty: Black Ops 2 remains one of the most ambitious games in the series to date, offering spectacular multiplayer modes that gave players better control of their loadouts. Its maps were some of the very best, including Raid, Hijacked, and Slums, which players happily ran through time after time. The zombies mode was more ambitious than before, with Mob of the Dead and Origins DLC providing additional zombie maps on top of the ones that shipped on the disc. Black Ops 2 featured a branching narrative with multiple endings, allowing players to decide who lived and died as the team went up against Raul Menendez, one of the most believable villains in franchise history. It also imagined life in 2025, more than a decade after the game’s release date. Overall, the title is a high point for the franchise. It’s a minor tragedy that newer players have no idea what they’ve been missing.
3 Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare
Released: Nov. 4, 2016

Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare had massive battles. In space. It had advanced technology and the firefights you know and love, this time with zero gravity. In space. And it had a compelling, surprisingly intimate plot featuring the voice talents of Brian Bloom and Kit Harington. They probably didn’t record them in space, even if it sounded like it. Besides all of that, some copies of the game shipped with Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered as a bonus, which made a good thing even better. For me and some other players, it was the last time a new Call of Duty game felt like a proper event that was not to be missed. The game’s continued absence from the Game Pass lineup is a real disappointment.
2 Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 Campaign Remastered
Released: Apr. 30, 2020

If you say “No Russian” to Call of Duty players of a certain age, they’ll immediately know just what you mean, perhaps even if they didn’t play the original Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2. The scene where that pivotal phrase was uttered ranks among the most memorable ever featured in a first-person shooter. At the time, it was preceded by a warning to let players know they were about to go to a very dark place. But that scene – and the game as a whole – were a welcome gut-punch in a campaign that pushed harder than its predecessor had dared. Besides the campaign, the multiplayer featured a big swing for the fences in the form of a tactical nuke the player could summon after earning 25 kills without dying, which naturally became nearly everyone’s goal in every match. What’s more, the main theme was composed by Hollywood legend Hans Zimmer, and the game added a cooperative mode known as Special Ops. Simply put, the game had everything. It’s a real shame Game Pass is missing such a classic, especially when it would be so easy to make Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 Campaign Remastered available and let players experience the story with touched up visuals.
1 Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered
Released: June 27, 2017

With 2007’s Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare, Infinity Ward proved the franchise had legs that could carry it far beyond World War 2. Set in the present time, the game imagined horrifying events that astonished players at each turn. You never knew what might happen next, and the twists kept you playing alongside a group of heroes that began to feel almost like family. Not only that, but the multiplayer mode was astonishingly compelling, providing tight corridors reminiscent of GoldenEye in some places, but more open in others. There wasn’t anything else quite like it at the time, and players spent hundreds of hours in deathmatch, practicing until they knew every tile on every ruined floor, every brick in each pile of rubble. Ten years later, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered brought much of that back, first as part of a special edition bundle for Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare and then as a standalone release the next year. It brought along a fresh coat of paint so the aging game didn’t look so old on newer monitors, providing the best way to play the game many consider to be the finest in the series. It totally belongs on Game Pass.

articles.headline: Where the top 2028 contenders are heading ahead of the midterm elections
keyFacts: Several potential 2028 presidential contenders are traveling to multiple states to campaign ahead of the midterm elections.
Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez campaigned in Michigan and donated $1 million to Senate candidate Abdul el Sayed.
Vice President JD Vance and Governor Gavin Newsom will hold campaign events in North Carolina and California next week.
body: Several top 2028 presidential contenders are traveling to various states ahead of the midterm elections . Here is where they will be from now to next week.
Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) hosted three campaign events in Michigan for Senate candidate Abdul el Sayed on Friday. Her last stop of the day was a “Latinos for Abdul” rally in Detroit.
As she toured Michigan, Ocasio-Cortez donated $1 million to el Sayed’s campaign. The two are ideologically aligned because of their progressive beliefs.
Vice President JD Vance is set to travel to North Carolina on Monday to hold campaign events in Asheville and Hendersonville. President Donald Trump will be in the state the following day.
Beyond in-person appearances, Vance will be on television for a town hall hosted by CBS News. The pretaped interview is scheduled to air at 8 p.m. Saturday.

Gov. Gavin Newsom (D-CA) will be across the country in New Hampshire on Saturday to show support for the state’s Democratic candidates. He is visiting Nashua, Exeter, Concord, and Manchester all in one day.

After the weekend trip, Newsom is expected to hold several campaign events in California next week. The focus of these events is on helping Democrats secure competitive congressional districts that were redrawn after voters approved Proposition 50 last November.
Instead of campaigning, Gov. Andy Beshear (D-KY) will be promoting his book, Go and Do Likewise: How We Heal a Broken Country , in Beverly Hills, California, next Friday.
Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-GA) will appear at a campaign rally on Saturday in Cobb County, Georgia , where he will be joined by Democratic gubernatorial candidate Keisha Lance Bottoms .

Ossoff is focusing on his reelection campaign against Rep. Mike Collins (R-GA). Earlier this week, Ossoff said he has “zero interest” in a 2028 presidential run if he’s reelected to the Senate this fall.

Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg is scheduled to appear on Saturday in Matthews, North Carolina, where he will be canvassing for former North Carolina Democratic Gov. Roy Cooper as Cooper runs for the Senate. Buttigieg will then head to two more events in Charlotte that day.

On Monday, Buttigieg will be holding a get-out-the-vote rally for Democratic candidates in Henrico County, Virginia . And on Wednesday, he will be participating in a virtual town hall concerning dark money in Montana .

Govs. Josh Shapiro (D-PA) and JB Pritzker (D-IL), two other potential 2028 presidential candidates, don’t have specific travel plans confirmed for this weekend or next week.

articles.headline: Trump stands by Susie Wiles as knives come out at White House before midterms
keyFacts: President Trump denied reports that he plans to replace White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, stating she will not be fired.
Insiders expect Trump will blame senior staff if Republicans perform poorly in the upcoming midterm elections.
Trump and his administration are expected to face Democratic investigations that could lead to impeachment if Republicans lose the midterms.
body: WASHINGTON — President Trump sought to put to rest two days of speculation that he might replace White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, saying Friday there is “zero chance” of her firing and that Wiles is “going to be here for a long time.”

Wiles, who was declared cancer-free last month after working through medical treatments, is regularly introduced by Trump as the world’s most powerful woman and the person most responsible for returning him to the White House, but she nonetheless found her fate the talk of Washington this week.

Politico’s influential Playbook newsletter reported on Thursday that Trump was asking allies for their thoughts on who might be a suitable replacement for Wiles — unleashing a swirl of rumors and campaigning as the chief of staff appeared to be on the ropes.
Trump called the report “fake news” on Friday, adding, “I could not be more happy with Susie.”
A close outside adviser to Trump told The Post that “I can tell when he is being genuine, and he really meant that.”

Wiles is widely credited with bringing stability and cohesion to the West Wing staff after the four years of Trump’s first term were consumed by ceaseless personnel drama and speculation about the next aide to be fired.

In a sign that Wiles’ power might be waning, Trump made an on-the-spot job offer last Friday to Katie Zacharia to be press secretary. Wiles was aware that Trump was courting Zacharia, but she was not part of the interview and had not pushed for her candidacy.

Zacharia was out of a job this Friday after fewer than five days of work following an unsteady 14-minute press briefing on Tuesday and a series of unflattering appearances on Fox News — giving an implicit boost to Wiles due to the fact she bore no responsibility for the hasty hiring.
Wiles and other senior Trump allies have been the subject of intrigue as insiders expect that Trump will want to blame someone if Republicans perform poorly in the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
The president is not expected to blame himself after barnstorming the country, trying to defy bleak polling by turning out his base of supporters.

“Trump is getting restless and once [he] feels he is losing, he always takes control,” a former senior Trump aide told The Post shortly before the president affirmed his support for the chief. “[If] Susie was smart she would leave and go make money without a DJT problem.”

Last week, Trump publicly fumed over the revelation that two leaders of the MAGA Inc. super PAC, Chris LaCivita and James Blair, took time out from the US campaign to visit the pro-Russian Republika Srpska in Bosnia and Herzegovina for a well-paid side hustle.

That junket gave the appearance that Trump’s team was diverting their attention from his own political fate. If Republicans lose the midterms, Trump, his administration and his family are expected to face dogged Democratic investigations that could lead to his third impeachment.
After LaCivita and Blair’s trip was revealed, subsequent reports noted that Wiles’ daughter, Katie, had also recently traveled to the Bosnian territory.
LaCivita ran Trump’s 2024 comeback campaign alongside Wiles, and Blair served as her deputy in the West Wing until April, describing himself as her “junkyard dog.”

Although LaCivita and Blair have been close to Wiles, many insiders described their one-time alliance as fractured. Others described a complex blame game emerging as key Trump lieutenants are looking out for their jobs and reputations in anticipation of massive fallout if Republicans lose the midterms.
“All the infighting [is] so so great two weeks ahead of midterms,” one administration official exclaimed.

Meanwhile, speculation is mounting about who might want to replace Wiles, including federal housing official Bill Pulte, who frequently travels on Air Force One and recently served as acting intelligence director, and deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller.

Longtime Wiles critics, such as Corey Lewandowski, are circling. The ex-campaign aide who was driven out of the Department of Homeland Security with Kristi Noem has been pushing for Pulte, according to the Washington Post, though Lewandowski has denied such conversations with Trump.

Sources inside and close to the White House said that they view Wiles’ daughter’s work as possible fodder for further attacks alleging corruption — after Wiles earned a reputation as an exception to allegations of self-dealing among top aides in Trump’s second term.
“Stephen Miller might feel it is finally his time and start really cutting at the ‘Susie’ squad,” an insider said.

Another said, however, that it’s possible Republicans will beat expectations, keeping losses low in the House and retaining the Senate, adding, “As long as she wants the job, I think she could have it.”

Some Republican sources argue that staff would not be blamed for an election wipeout, pointing to the effects of the longer-than-anticipated Iran war, which has spurred voter frustrations with higher energy prices, rising inflation and increased interest rates.
“Anyone with even a modicum of honest self reflection would admit that the driving force behind potential GOP midterm losses is the war in Iran,” said a source close to the White House.

“It split the president’s coalition, reminded swing voters that the administration wasn’t focusing on their domestic concerns and most importantly triggered a rise in gas prices. It’s ironic to me that so many of the voices in elite conservative media circles lamenting our current political predicament were also some of the biggest cheerleaders for bombing Iran.”

articles.headline: Replit is no longer working with Anthropic, CEO says
keyFacts: Replit CEO Amjad Masad stated that the platform is no longer working with Anthropic, citing cost, partnership, and performance reasons.
Replit previously used Anthropic's models to run its platform, but an unnamed insider disputed Masad's claim and said the partnership remains active.
TechCrunch reached out to Replit for clarification and reported that it will update the story if it hears back.
body: Replit, the AI coding platform that has become a favorite of startup founders and developers, is no longer working with Anthropic, the company’s CEO and co-founder Amjad Masad said Thursday while onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt.

Masad said the decision was made for a number of different reasons, including cost. Replit announced a partnership with OpenAI in August, but there was never any indication that it was no longer with Anthropic.

“I think ChatGPT is better now,” Masad said, adding that the company uses an internal benchmark to help assess metrics like performance. “We publish a public benchmark as well, and consistently, Sol and Astra perform better on building vibe-coded applications from scratch. It was a decision based on both cost, partnership, and performance. And for all these reasons, we just felt like they were a better partner for now.”

Replit sells a cloud-based software development platform where users can develop and deploy apps directly from inside their browser. Under its partnership with Anthropic, Replit used the AI lab’s Claude models to run its platform. That partnership was said to have helped the company grow its revenue significantly.

Masad’s comments were rejected by insiders familiar with the partnership between the Anthropic and Replit, however. One person familiar, who asked not to be named, said the partnership was still in place.

There is evidence on the company’s website, blog posts, and social media posts that Replit was using Anthropic products as recently as a few weeks ago. For instance, a blog post in late September cites Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5 and Claude Fable 5.1 as models running in Replit Agent’s production environment. Around the same time, one of Replit’s product employees posted on X about using Anthropic’s flagship model Opus 5.5 and promoting its capabilities.
TechCrunch reached back out to Replit for clarification and will update this story if we hear back.
Masad shared insights about the company’s growth while onstage at Disrupt, noting that enterprise is starting to provide a larger slice of revenue.

“We’re not sharing ARR numbers just yet, but in terms of growth, like, I would say, enterprise was like 2% of revenue last year,” Masad said. “This year, I would say like 15% of our revenue is enterprise contracts, and more than 50% of our revenue is B2B.”
Masad also commented on the necessity for good AI safety measures.

“In the same way that us humans need a certain environment to work — you need a nice office, maybe nice good food in the office, air-conditioning, computer — agents need a habitat for them to exist and do good work,” he said. “So that habitat has good orchestration, good error recovery, good safety and security and sandboxing, good networking, good identity and authorization. And once you figure all of that out, then you can deploy AI safely.”
This article was updated to article to include more context on Replit using Anthropic’s models.

articles.headline: Tish James confronted on camera over Trump's accusation of bias in Cornell rape case
keyFacts: New York Attorney General Letitia James promised an impartial investigation into seven defendants accused of sexual assault at Cornell University.
Donald Trump and defense attorneys have demanded James be removed from the case, accusing her of bias toward the alleged victim.
Governor Hochul and James rejected bias claims, stating the investigation into the fraternity party assault will be guided strictly by evidence.
body: New York Attorney General Letitia James on Friday vowed to conduct a "fair" investigation into the seven defendants accused of sexually assaulting an unnamed woman at a fraternity party at Cornell University.

James’ investigation into the alleged college gang rape was launched after the filing of a recent lawsuit against Cornell University, the Chi Phi fraternity and several other defendants that has thrust the Ivy League university’s handling of campus sexual assault into the national spotlight.
The remarks to a reporter come as James has repeatedly pushed back on questions about her impartiality, insisting the investigation will be guided by the facts and evidence, not politics.

President Donald Trump, a longtime foe of the attorney general, has also questioned James' ability to lead an impartial investigation. Trump made the remarks after Fox News' Peter Doocy asked for his view on Hochul appointing James as special prosecutor in the case.
LETITIA JAMES FACES NEW PUSH TO BOOT HER FROM CORNELL RAPE PROBE OVER ALLEGED BIAS: COURT DOCUMENTS

"Letitia James is a corrupt person," Trump said. "She’s totally corrupt, and I can’t imagine it. And I feel badly for whoever she’s looking at because they won’t get a fair shake. Letitia James is a corrupt person."

Attorneys for two of the defendants have also sought James’ removal, including Andrew Miltenberg, who represents Gillio Lopes, and Teny Geragos, who represents Winston Lee. The defense attorneys point to a social media post by James that Geragos separately argued in a court filing shows she is "unquestionably biased."
Just days before Hochul's appointment, James posted on X in support of the alleged victim, identified in court filings as Jane Doe.

"What this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable. I’m holding her in my heart and in my prayers," James posted on X Sept. 28. "To her, and to all survivors: you’re not alone. We stand with you."
Hochul has stood by her appointment of James amid the criticism, saying she has "every confidence" the attorney general will "look at the facts, examine the record and draw the proper conclusions."

James has rejected accusations that she prejudged the case, saying during an attorney general campaign debate that her comments supporting the alleged victim were intended to demonstrate "empathy" and insisting that "politics stops at the door" of her office.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

The case centers on allegations from a Cornell student that she was gang raped at a Chi Phi fraternity house party in 2024. Her allegations were investigated by Cornell University Police, which submitted her six-page sworn statement to the Tompkins County District Attorney’s Office.
Prosecutors declined to pursue charges at the time, concluding that the conduct described in the statement did not provide sufficient evidence to sustain criminal charges under New York law.

Cornell separately conducted a Title IX investigation that resulted in disciplinary action against several of the seven defendants, including the expulsion of two students and suspension of two others.

articles.headline: Ranking the Premier League's all-time greatest super subs
keyFacts: Jermain Defoe was ranked as the Premier League's greatest super sub for scoring a record 24 goals off the bench.
The rankings evaluated players on their consistent goal and assist contributions as Premier League substitutes.
Nwankwo Kanu, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Edin Dzeko, and Javier Hernandez rounded out the top five spots.
body: - Published
Mikel Arteta may be attempting to rebrand them "finishers" but there's only one phrase in the footballing lexicon to sum up today's focus: super subs.
Yes, we're looking for those players renowned for making a devastating impact off the bench, those guaranteed game-changers a manager turns to when in desperate need of a goal.

First, an honorary mention for some who missed out, such as one-season wonder Adam le Fondre, who holds the record for the most goals off the bench in a single Premier League campaign - five of his eight came in a three-game spell in January 2013.

Hernan Crespo boasts the best goals-per-game ratio but his six in 16 substitute appearances for Chelsea represents a small sample size, likewise ex-Norwich and Leicester forward Mark Robins with five in 14 outings as a replacement.
To make the all-time top 10 Premier League super subs, players need to have consistently delivered throughout their careers, providing goals and assists.
So here we go, I've ranked mine below - you can have your say in the comments, too.
10. Theo Walcott
Theo Walcott, replaced on 168 occasions, holds the record as the most subbed off player in Premier League history. Yet it's his impact coming on to the pitch we're interested in here.

Bursting on to the top-flight scene as an explosive teenager, the flying forward was often used by Arsenal boss Arsene Wenger to stretch defences with his pace and movement - a lactic acid-inducing sight for flailing full-backs.
The England international pieced together an impressive substitute CV throughout his Premier League career.

No-one has more than Walcott's 14 assists as a sub - Ryan Giggs and Marc Albrighton are level - while he also scored 10 goals as a replacement across his time with the Gunners, Everton and Southampton.
It puts him fourth on the list for overall goal contributions off the bench.
9. Victor Anichebe
This was a toss up between Victor Anichebe and Divock Origi, with both forwards contributing exactly half of all their Premier League goals as a substitute.

Ex-Everton, West Brom and Sunderland striker Anichebe edges it having notched a couple more - a tally of 13 placing the former Nigeria international in joint-eighth on the all-time list - while he also chipped in with five assists off the bench.
Roman Pavlyuchenko was also unlucky to miss out - 45% of his 20 Premier League goals came as a substitute for Tottenham.
8. Daniel Sturridge
There's a good case for Danny Welbeck, who as the only current player in the top three, with 19 goals, still has time to catch those above him.
Welbeck was a goalscoring sub at Manchester United and Arsenal but perfected the art on the south coast, with 12 of his tally coming during six years with Brighton.
The 35-year-old is now at Chelsea but - with apologies to Danny - there is another former Blue whose stats demand a place on this list.
Daniel Sturridge has two fewer substitute goals then Welbeck but has scored a slightly higher percentage of his overall Premier League tally as a sub - 22%.
The former England man, who played for Manchester City, Chelsea, Bolton, Liverpool and West Brom in the top flight, was good for an assist, too.
In fact, when you take his total goal contributions of 24, he provided at a more prolific rate than every substitute in Premier League history - bar Edin Dzeko and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.
Richarlison matches Sturridge for minutes per goal contribution, but with eight fewer the Brazilian, perhaps harshly, misses out.
7. Olivier Giroud
A World Cup and Champions League winner, one of the few trophies Olivier Giroud hasn't got his hands on is the Premier League title despite a knack for scoring important goals off the bench.

The Frenchman is second on the all-time substitute scoring list, accounting for 21 of his 90 top-flight goals - that's almost a quarter - with only Dzeko, Solskjaer and Javier Hernandez boasting a better minutes-per-goal record as a sub.
Giroud honed his ability to make a late impact at Arsenal and Chelsea, making 103 substitute appearances in total across 10 seasons in the Premier League.
6. Tore Andre Flo

Good feet for a big man. Tore Andre Flo was a menace for Premier League defenders not merely because of his tall, gangly frame but for the silky touches the Norwegian often showed with his giant boots.
Flo scored 34% of his 38 Premier League goals as a substitute - the eighth-highest ratio for those with 20 top-flight goals or more, while he is also joint-eighth overall for goals from a substitute.
The first of those came just three minutes into his Chelsea debut in 1997, and it was with the Blues he enjoyed his best Premier League output before a later stint at Sunderland.
Having also provided three assists as a sub, he ranks fifth for minutes-per-goal involvements, contributing to his side scoring once every 78 minutes on average when used off the bench.
5. Javier Hernandez
The Little Pea. Small in stature but a giant headache for tiring defenders.

Of all players in Premier League history to have scored at least 10 goals as a substitute, only one - Sergio Aguero, and it feels a stretch to call the competition's sixth-highest scorer a super sub - has netted at a more prolific rate than Javier 'Chicharito' Hernandez.

He has 19 in 78 sub appearances, a rate of 0.24 per game, with 36% of all his Premier League goals coming after he started on the bench - predominantly for Manchester United but also later in his career at West Ham.
He netted on average every 88 minutes when used as a replacement.

Indeed, only Jermain Defoe and Giroud have scored more goals as a substitute than the Mexican, while he sits among a leading group of seven - including Defoe - who have scored five match-winners as a sub.
4. Edin Dzeko
Aged 40, Edin Dzeko is still scoring goals for Bundesliga outfit Schalke. His record as a substitute in the Premier League, however, remains among the greatest.
Dzeko netted 50 Premier League goals for Manchester City, with more than a quarter of those coming as a substitute.

Only Aguero and Hernandez, of players to have scored at least 10 goals as a sub, have better goals-per-game ratios than him. When you break it down to minutes per goal, Dzeko is level at the top with Solskjaer - scoring on average every 83 minutes.
He stands alone once you add assists, too - 17 goal contributions during 56 top-flight games as a replacement means Dzeko returned on average every 63 minutes.

The most important of those goals, of course, came in stoppage time against QPR on the final day of the 2012 season. Everyone remembers the Aguero moment, but it was substitute Dzeko's header two minutes earlier that levelled the game.
3. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer
Ole Gunnar Solskjaer is perhaps the most iconic of super subs, largely for that Treble-clinching night in Barcelona.

The baby-faced Norwegian, having started Manchester United's FA Cup final win over Newcastle four days earlier, came on in the 81st minute of the Champions League final to toe-poke a stoppage-time winner after Teddy Sheringham had equalised against Bayern Munich moments earlier.
It capped a vintage few months for Solskjaer's super sub legend, having bagged four in the final 10 minutes of an 8-1 win at Nottingham Forest in the February.

Sticking strictly to his Premier League output, Solskjaer is joint-fifth on the all-time substitute scoring list with 17, netting 19% of his 91 top-flight goals off the bench, with a ratio of 0.2 goals-per-game as a sub.

His rate of scoring on average once every 83 minutes off the bench is a competition high that can only be matched by Dzeko. The caveat is, like Dzeko, Solskjaer was playing for one of the most dominant teams in the land.
2. Nwankwo Kanu
Nwankwo Kanu's impact as a substitute was felt immediately at Arsenal.

Coming off the bench on his debut, the Nigerian forward collected a throw-in meant for a Sheffield United player - after the opposition kicked the ball out for an injury - and crossed for Marc Overmars to score. It sparked a famous FA Cup rematch.
In the Premier League, he was just as ruthless. Kanu, who joined from Inter Milan having earlier won the Champions League at Ajax, made 56 of his 119 top-flight appearances for Arsenal as a sub.
When you take in spells at West Brom and Portsmouth, too, he netted 17 goals off the bench - 31% of all his top-flight strikes - which places him joint-fifth on the all-time substitute scoring list.
But he was almost as prolific at creating them, making 12 assists as a substitute - a tally only bettered by three players in Premier League history.
1. Jermain Defoe
OK, goals are currency and Jermain Defoe has netted more as a substitute than any other Premier League player.

Remarkably, the 24 he scored when coming on all came in different fixtures - which, of course, means he has also scored in more games as a substitute than anyone else. And, as mentioned, a league-high five of those were match-winners.

He scored six times as a substitute in his debut Premier League season, earning West Ham a 3-2 win at Ipswich with his first top-flight goal, and netted for the final time in the competition 17 years later after coming on to rescue Bournemouth a stoppage-time point at Watford.

Simply put, throughout his career, Defoe - also England's highest-scoring substitute with seven goals - was the ruthless finisher a manager wished to see when anxiously glancing at their bench in need of a goal.

articles.headline: MapQuest App Shows You Where License Plate Readers Are in Your Area
keyFacts: MapQuest added a feature showing the locations, types, and coordinates of automatic license plate readers.
Users can view the cameras by opening the MapQuest app and turning on the Surveillance option under Layers.
Civil liberties groups said data collected by license plate readers helps create a mass surveillance network that tracks everyone.
body: The roads have eyes, and MapQuest can now show you where they are. The navigational app added a feature this week that lets you discover where Flock cameras and other automatic license plate readers are in your neighborhood and beyond.

In a post on Bluesky, MapQuest said its app shows locations of license plate readers from Flock and many other companies — Motorola Solutions (Vigilant), Genetec, Axis Communications, Axon, Leonardo (ELSAG), Neology, Rekor, PlateSmart, Ubicquia, Verkada and more.

To activate the feature, open the MapQuest app, tap the Layers icon and turn on the Surveillance option. You will then see tiny eyeballs on the map that indicate where license plate readers are located. If you click on an eyeball, it will show what type of license plate reader it is — dome or fixed, for example — and the exact coordinates.
More from CNET

MapQuest has been riding a wave of relevance, years after being relegated to lower-tier status by the likes of Google, Apple and Waze. In August, MapQuest refused to change Lake Ontario to Lake America in its maps despite President Donald Trump’s executive order. It then muscled into Android Auto to give drivers an alternative to Google Maps on their dashboards.

But MapQuest isn’t the first app to reveal locations of license plate readers. The others include DeFlock, FlockHopper, Pelican and LPR Maps. Some of them rely on crowdsourcing — drivers notify the app when they believe they have spotted a license plate reader and where it is.
Read more: How to Tell if a New Neighborhood Device Is a Flock Surveillance Camera
MapQuest didn’t say how it knows where license plate readers are located, and a representative didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

Although license plate readers have been around for decades and there are more than 140,000 all over the US, the technology has become highly unpopular. Flock cameras can collect a huge trove of data from a car: license plate, the make, model and color, and its location. Civil liberties groups and others say that all this information — input into law enforcement databases across the country — helps to create a mass surveillance network that can track everyone, not just suspected criminals.
There have been instances of Flock data being misused, such as police officers stalking ex-spouses and girlfriends, and people being wrongly pulled over and accused of stealing their cars.

License plate readers are also used for more mundane operations, such as electronic toll collection on roads and bridges, traffic violations, parking enforcement, vehicle repossessions and parking gate activation for access to restricted areas.
I’m surrounded by license plate readers
I tried the new MapQuest feature. Being more of a Google Maps person, I didn’t have the MapQuest app, so I installed it on my phone.

I opened the app, found the Surveillance layer and turned it on. I was greeted by a bunch of eyeballs on the map in my city and county. I clicked on several of them and saw their coordinates and what type they were — dome, fixed, pan/tilt and so on — but I didn’t see the names of the companies that own them.
But at least now I know which streets have eyes on me.
